text:
maya: heads-up — dashboard spike on structured invoke rejects this morning; a lot of requests are routing to degen-route because fn-invoke validation flagged them as 'shape_noise'. :eyes:
andrew: ugh, logs? sample ts? can you paste a sample payload?
maya: here's a redacted example:
```
{"user_id": "acct_123", "prompt": "summarize...", "tools": [{"name":"search","args": null}], "fn_response": "{...}"}
```
chris: that null args for tools looks like it's tripping the fncall validator; our soft-validate is classifying as REJECT and routing to degen. that's billing-heavy.
irene: seeing the same on panel 'invoke->rejections->by_reason' — +470% in last 30m. link: https://console/redwood/dashboards/invoke_rejects (internal)
infra-bot: alert: invoke-validator-reject-rate exceeded threshold in eu-west-1 at 7750012000
andrew: quick mitigation: can we tag these as 'soft_reject' not 'hard' so routing policy doesn't flip to degen? also add a sampling flag to avoid double billing.
chris: agree. I can change the router to prefer fallback_model only when validator.score < 0.2. for now, prefer original model with degraded QoS.
maya: I'll add telemetry field `validation_hint`="nullable-tool-args" and send a small sample to S3 + create a runbook entry.
irene: also update the dashboard to surface the new hint field and a per-route cost estimate so support can triage.
andrew: can we do a quick canary: ship change to canary-hosted for 1% traffic this afternoon? if green, roll to 25%.
chris: plan sounds good. i'll open the PR for router policy and add unit tests for null-tool args.
maya: PR link: https://git/redwood/pull/1234 — I'll own the telemetry + dashboard patch.
irene: tagging @console-team FYI
maya: thanks — i'll post a postmortem if we hit broader spike :thumbsup:
